examples.title: Canonicalise an archive from any producer
Pin one release timestamp instead of the DOS epoch

description: Make ANY archive reproducible: zipnative's canonicalizeZip() rewrites a Gradle, Maven, zip, Explorer or 7-Zip archive into the canonical deterministic form zipnative itself writes — entries sorted by raw name bytes, one timestamp (the DOS epoch, or a pinned `date`, read as UTC), the UTF-8 flag on every name, no extra field but Zip64, the constant version-made-by, no data descriptor — WITHOUT recompressing a payload (the compressed bytes travel bit for bit; nothing is decoded, so the result is identical on every runtime). Idempotent: canonicalising the result again returns the same bytes (summary.alreadyCanonical). Entry names and payloads travel verbatim (a corrupt or unsafe entry stays so — run verify_zip first when integrity matters). summary.canonicalForm is the engine's own analyzeDeterminism() verdict on the output. keepComments (default false) and keepExternalAttributes (default true) choose what survives. Duplicate-name archives are refused. Verify with inspect_zip { check:['canonical-form'], canonicalDate } and compare summary.sha256 across builds.

date.description: The one timestamp written on every entry (ISO-8601, 1980-01-01 … 2107-12-31, read as UTC; 2-second DOS granularity). Default: the DOS epoch 1980-01-01T00:00:00 — the deterministic default. Pass the same value to inspect_zip `canonicalDate` to verify the result.

includeSha256.description: Add `summary.sha256` of the produced bytes (the reproducibility proof to compare across builds).

keepComments.description: Keep the archive comment and the entry comments (default false: the canonical form carries none).

keepExternalAttributes.description: Keep each entry's external attributes — Unix modes, DOS attributes (default true); false writes the canonical defaults (0o100644 files, 0o40755 directories).

limits.description: Per-call override of zipnative's security bounds (CWE-400/409); absent keys keep the engine defaults (describe_engine.defaultLimits). A value above its operator ceiling is LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED. Raise only for trusted input.

maxEntryCompressedSize.description: Bytes, one compressed payload fetched by the byte-range reader (access range).

outputMode.description: 'base64' (default): inline embedded resource (≤ 50 MiB; the bytes appear in both its data: uri and its blob). 'file': written into the sandbox (never overwrites; ≤ ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_FILE_OUTPUT_BYTES, default 4 GiB) and returned as a resource_link — far fewer tokens.

outputPath.description: Relative path inside the sandbox (only when outputMode='file'); must end in a container extension (.zip recommended).

strict.description: Turn the first engine diagnostic into a ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC error.

zipBase64.description: Archive bytes, base64 (≤ 128 MiB decoded). Exclusive with zipPath.

zipPath.description: Archive path relative to the ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (container extensions: .zip .jar .docx .epub …). Exclusive with zipBase64; saves re-sending bytes between calls.

name: canonicalize_zip

outputSchema.description: Archive result: base64 mode = an embedded `resource` block (not repeated here); file mode = `filePath` + a resource_link.

diagnostics.description: Non-fatal engine concerns (de-duplicated by code + entry, ≤ 200; codes in describe_engine.diagnosticCodes). Empty for a clean archive.

diagnosticsTruncated.description: true when rows beyond 200 were dropped.

alreadyCanonical.description: true when the input already was in this canonical form (the output bytes equal the input bytes).

canonicalForm.description: zipnative's analyzeDeterminism() verdict on the output, with the same pinned date — true for every successful rewrite.

pinnedDate.description: The timestamp every entry carries (ISO-8601, UTC); null for the DOS epoch.

title: Canonicalise archive (reproducible, no recompression)
